gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Thin, angular and a bit sci-fi: that is Megrim. But Noto Sans Elbasan is the one built for sustained reading, a plain sans with large lowercase forms and terminals that stay open, while Megrim is happiest holding a pen-steady line up top.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic reads open and clean, with ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Shrink Megrim down, though, and its marker-nib line, which ignores direction, loses the presence that suits large sizes, while the sans below stays comfortable at any scale.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Megrim, angular and futuristic, draws without any pressure swells, so the eye never slows down on it. Noto Sans Ethiopic does the opposite job well, a sturdy, tall sans-serif lowercase with hanging c terminals made for steady reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Futuristic and sharp, Megrim has a texture like neatly bent pipe cleaner. Noto Sans Georgian is the one that handles the actual reading, with open curves throughout and short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Megrim draws its angular, futuristic strokes at one weight. That makes it best as a display voice, while Noto Sans Glagolitic, a sturdy sans-serif with open round letters, is the one that stays clear when text gets small.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Megrim's stroke never varies in thickness, which gives it a hard, futuristic edge. Noto Sans Gothic handles the quieter work, a sans-serif whose lowercase counters are big as drilled glass beads and whose round forms read like open parentheses.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Professional in manner, Noto Sans Grantha has tall little letters like flattened pen-nib bowls, so reading never snags on a closed-up shape. But Megrim does the showier job as a display face, with crossbars as thick as its stems and an angular, futuristic edge.
